title: The persona claim block still lets two consumers correlate
description:
Pseudonyms are now per-consumer and unlinkable, but the token around them is not. hire-grpc/src/service.rs builds a persona claim block carrying root_trust_domain, sources, auth_methods and a whole-second attested_at. Those values are identical for any two consumers served in the same window.

So two colluding consumers holding different pseudonyms can still infer they are talking to the same person by comparing that tuple. attested_at at second granularity is the strongest of the four: it is effectively a join key for concurrent requests.

They cannot recover the root identity — that is fixed, and the log no longer carries the mapping either. This is correlation, not deanonymisation. But README, SPEC-HIRE and MOTIVATIONS all say two applications cannot work out they are talking to the same person, and as written that is now narrowly false.

Raised by the judge during persona-5s4b.41 and deliberately not fixed there: narrowing the claim block is a wire-format decision, and doing it inside a plumbing change would have been scope creep. The docs now state the residual explicitly rather than implying it is absent.

Options for whoever takes it: drop root_trust_domain (a consumer does not need it), coarsen or remove attested_at, and consider whether sources and auth_methods belong in a per-consumer token at all — they describe the human's environment, not the consumer's relationship to it. Note persona-ogiv wants attested_at to become MORE precise for freshness, which pulls the other way; the two need deciding together.
notes:
Resolved by owner decision during persona-ogiv, not by engineering. attested_at stays published at whole-second granularity: 'we are not going to delete it, otherwise there is no point. the spec and implementation can be honest about what it means, but we are not going to let the perfect be the enemy of the better.'

So freshness wins over unlinkability on this field, deliberately. The residual stands: two colluding consumers served in the same window see the same whole-second attested_at, the same root_trust_domain, sources and auth_methods, and can infer they are talking to one person even though their pseudonyms differ. Granularity is already as coarse as JWT works in, so there is no free reduction left on this field.

This bead is therefore ACCEPTED AND BOUNDED rather than open for a fix. What would still be worth doing is narrowing the OTHER three fields, which carry correlation without carrying freshness: root_trust_domain is not needed by a consumer, and sources and auth_methods describe the human's environment rather than the consumer's relationship to it.
close_reason: NOT OPEN FOR A FIX -- closed per the bead's own NOTES, which record an owner decision made during persona-ogiv: 'ACCEPTED AND BOUNDED rather than open for a fix'. Verified 2026-09-15 that the code still matches the state that decision was made about: hire-core/src/hvid.rs still carries pub root_trust_domain: String and pub auth_methods: Vec<String>, and attested_at remains whole-second. The residual correlation those fields permit was weighed and accepted; leaving the bead open invites someone to re-litigate a settled call. The related and still-live question -- whether pseudonyms are consumer-scoped or audience-scoped -- is tracked on persona-l879, which was updated today after pseudonym derivation landed.
